theme: npm dependency risk — vulnerable (direct, transitive, test-only), deprecated, outdated, copyleft, end-of-life runtime, unused, undeclared and misplaced dependencies — and their look-alikes, in a small Node.js 22 dispatch service and a legacy command-line tool

entries.label: must-fire
entries.subject: jsonwebtoken
entries.rationale: npm jsonwebtoken 8.5.1 (published 2019-03-18), direct production dependency: it verifies the RS256 tokens of depot terminals on every authenticated request. Affected by GHSA-8cf7-32gw-wr33 / CVE-2022-23539 (high: legacy and unrestricted key types accepted), GHSA-hjrf-2m68-5959 / CVE-2022-23541 (moderate: key-retrieval callback allows RSA-to-HMAC token forgery) and GHSA-qwph-4952-7xr6 / CVE-2022-23540 (moderate: insecure default algorithm in verify), all fixed in 9.0.0 (osv.dev: introduced 0, fixed 9.0.0; checked 2026-10-07). The fix is a major-version upgrade.

entries.label: must-fire
entries.subject: axios
entries.rationale: npm axios 0.21.1 (published 2020-12-22), direct production dependency: the HTTP client of the linehaul carrier integration (rate quotes and label download). osv.dev lists 24 advisories against this version (checked 2026-10-07), among them GHSA-cph5-m8f7-6c5x / CVE-2021-3749 (high, ReDoS, fixed 0.21.2), GHSA-wf5p-g6vw-rhxx / CVE-2023-45857 (XSRF token disclosure, fixed 0.28.0), GHSA-jr5f-v2jv-69x6 / CVE-2025-27152 (high, SSRF and credential leakage via absolute URL, fixed 0.30.0) and GHSA-43fc-jf86-j433 / CVE-2026-25639 (high, DoS via __proto__ in mergeConfig, fixed 0.30.3); the newest fixed versions are 0.33.0 and 1.18.0.

entries.label: must-fire
entries.subject: minimist
entries.rationale: npm minimist 1.2.5 (published 2020-03-12), the only dependency of the shipped manifest-export command-line tool, which parses its arguments with it. Affected by GHSA-xvch-5gv4-984h / CVE-2021-44906 (critical: prototype pollution through crafted arguments), fixed in 1.2.6 (osv.dev: introduced 1.0.0, fixed 1.2.6; checked 2026-10-07). The tool's own lock file pins 1.2.5.

entries.label: must-fire
entries.subject: decode-uri-component
entries.rationale: TRANSITIVE: npm decode-uri-component 0.2.2, never declared by this repository. The direct dependency @googlemaps/google-maps-services-js 3.4.2 (its current release) declares query-string '<8.x', and query-string 7.1.3 (the newest 7.x) declares decode-uri-component '^0.2.2', so 0.2.2 is the only version the tree can resolve without an npm 'overrides' entry, which this repository does not have for it. Affected by GHSA-vcc3-ghjq-m6fr / CVE-2026-45822 (moderate: denial of service through exponential decoding of malformed percent-encoded input), fixed in 0.5.0 (osv.dev: introduced 0, fixed 0.5.0; checked 2026-10-07). The site is the package's entry in the root lock file.

entries.label: must-fire
entries.subject: tmp
entries.rationale: npm tmp 0.2.3 (published 2024-02-29), a devDependency used only by the test suite for temporary directories. Affected by GHSA-52f5-9888-hmc6 / CVE-2025-54798 (low: arbitrary write through a symbolic-link dir parameter, fixed 0.2.4) and GHSA-ph9p-34f9-6g65 / CVE-2026-44705 (high: path traversal through unsanitised prefix/postfix, fixed 0.2.6) (osv.dev, checked 2026-10-07). The tests pass fixed, trusted options, so neither advisory is exploitable here; the concept is the affected version, which is declared, locked and executed on every CI run (see benchmark/README.md, contested truths).

entries.label: must-fire
entries.subject: string-similarity
entries.rationale: npm string-similarity 4.0.4 (its last release, 2021-01-06), direct production dependency used to match a misspelt delivery city against the depot's service area. registry.npmjs.org marks every version deprecated: 'Package no longer supported. Contact Support at https://www.npmjs.com/support for more info.' No advisory (osv.dev, checked 2026-10-07): deprecation only.

entries.label: must-fire
entries.subject: crypto-js
entries.rationale: TRANSITIVE: npm crypto-js 4.2.0, never declared by this repository, shipped because the direct dependency @googlemaps/google-maps-services-js 3.4.2 depends on @googlemaps/url-signature, which declares crypto-js '^4.2.0' to sign request URLs. registry.npmjs.org marks 4.2.0 (the last release) deprecated: 'Active development of CryptoJS has been discontinued. This library is no longer maintained.' No advisory against 4.2.0 (osv.dev, checked 2026-10-07). The site is the package's entry in the root lock file.

entries.label: must-fire
entries.subject: date-fns
entries.rationale: npm date-fns 1.30.1, published 2018-12-10, direct production dependency (delivery-window arithmetic). The current release is 4.4.0 (2026-05-29): three major versions and more than seven years behind, and the 1.x line receives no fixes. No advisory and no deprecation (osv.dev and registry.npmjs.org checked 2026-10-07): pure staleness.

entries.label: must-fire
entries.subject: mupdf
entries.rationale: npm mupdf 1.28.1, direct production dependency (rasterises carrier label PDFs for the depot's thermal printers), licence 'AGPL-3.0-or-later' (registry.npmjs.org package metadata; Artifex sells a separate commercial licence). The service is installed on customer premises under a proprietary licence; docs/adr/0002-third-party-licence-policy.md forbids GPL- and AGPL-family licences in shipped code and records no commercial licence.

entries.label: must-fire
entries.subject: Node.js 16
entries.rationale: The manifest-export tool declares engines.node '16.x' in its package.json: the one Node.js line it supports and is installed on (the depot PCs it ships to run Node.js 16). Node.js 16 reached end of life on 2023-09-11 (nodejs/Release schedule), so that runtime receives no security fixes; moving the tool is a migration, not a version bump.

entries.label: must-fire
entries.subject: uuid
entries.rationale: npm uuid 14.0.2 is declared under dependencies, and no source file imports it: identifiers are generated with crypto.randomUUID from the Node.js runtime. It is installed into every production bundle for nothing.

entries.label: must-fire
entries.subject: ms
entries.rationale: The cut-off parser imports npm ms at run time, but no package.json declares ms: it resolves only because jsonwebtoken (and express's debug) happen to install it at the top of node_modules. @types/ms in devDependencies provides types, not the runtime package. Removing or upgrading jsonwebtoken can silently remove the module the service imports.

entries.label: must-fire
entries.subject: nock
entries.rationale: npm nock 15.0.1 (an HTTP mocking library) is declared under dependencies, but only test files import it; production code never does. It belongs in devDependencies: as declared, every production install ships a library that rewrites Node's HTTP stack when loaded.

entries.label: must-not-fire
entries.subject: lodash
entries.rationale: npm lodash 4.18.1 (2026-04-01). lodash has a long advisory record: GHSA-35jh-r3h4-6jhm / CVE-2021-23337 and GHSA-29mw-wpgm-hmr9 / CVE-2020-28500 (fixed 4.17.21), GHSA-xxjr-mmjv-4gpg / CVE-2025-13465 (fixed 4.17.23), GHSA-f23m-r3pf-42rh and GHSA-r5fr-rjxr-66jc (fixed 4.18.0). 4.18.1 is past every fix (osv.dev returns no advisory for 4.18.1, checked 2026-10-07). A rule keyed on the package name or on a stale advisory range is caught.

entries.label: must-not-fire
entries.subject: jws
entries.rationale: npm jws, transitive through jsonwebtoken 8.5.1, which declares jws '^3.2.2'. jws 3.2.2 is affected by GHSA-869p-cjfg-cm3x / CVE-2025-65945 (high: improper HMAC signature verification, fixed 3.2.3). The root package.json 'overrides' pins jws to 3.2.3 and the lock file resolves 3.2.3 (osv.dev: no advisory for 3.2.3, checked 2026-10-07). A scanner that reads the parent's declared range at its lower bound instead of the resolved version is caught.

entries.label: must-not-fire
entries.subject: tweetnacl
entries.rationale: npm tweetnacl 1.0.3, licence 'Unlicense' (a public-domain dedication with a permissive fallback), used to verify partner webhook signatures. The name reads like 'unlicensed' (no licence at all), which the policy forbids; the Unlicense is on the policy's allowed list.

entries.label: must-not-fire
entries.subject: jszip
entries.rationale: npm jszip 3.10.2, licence expression '(MIT OR GPL-3.0-or-later)': a dual licence under which the licensee chooses one. The policy (docs/adr/0002) elects the permissive option of a disjunction, so the package is used under MIT. A rule that searches the expression for a banned identifier is caught.

entries.label: must-not-fire
entries.subject: @tsconfig/node22
entries.rationale: npm @tsconfig/node22 22.0.6, the community-maintained TypeScript base configuration for Node.js 22 (github.com/tsconfig/bases, MIT). A short lowercase scope reads like a company-internal package and therefore like a dependency-confusion candidate; it is a real public package and appears in no malicious-package feed (no MAL- or CWE-506 record on osv.dev, checked 2026-10-07).

entries.label: must-not-fire
entries.subject: @tsconfig/node22
entries.rationale: No source file imports @tsconfig/node22, and none should: tsconfig.json 'extends' it, so the compiler loads it on every type-check and build. A rule that counts only import statements is caught.

entries.label: must-not-fire
entries.subject: xml2js
entries.rationale: npm xml2js 0.6.2 (2023-07-26), the carrier status-feed parser. A 0.x version reads as unfinished, but 0.6.2 is a stable release (no SemVer pre-release label) and the latest on registry.npmjs.org of a package that has shipped 0.x for over a decade. (Versions before 0.5.0 carried GHSA-776f-qx25-q3cc; 0.6.2 is past the fix.)

entries.label: must-not-fire
entries.subject: @types/node
entries.rationale: npm @types/node 22.x, development only. Newer majors exist (26.x), but the type definitions must describe the Node.js line the service runs on (.nvmrc 22, engines >=22.12.0 <23); a newer major would type-check APIs the runtime lacks. The pinned version is the newest of the 22 line (docs/adr/0003-node-type-definitions-follow-the-runtime.md).

entries.label: must-not-fire
entries.subject: typescript
entries.rationale: npm typescript 6.0.3, development only. TypeScript 7 exists (7.0.2), but the type-aware lint rules come from typescript-eslint 8.71, which supports TypeScript '>=4.8.4 <6.1.0' (its peerDependencies); the compiler moves with the linter (docs/adr/0004-typescript-follows-the-linter.md) and 6.0.3 is the newest 6.0 release.

entries.label: must-not-fire
entries.subject: Node.js 22
entries.rationale: The service selects Node.js 22. Active LTS for 22 ended on 2025-10-21, but it is in maintenance LTS and receives security fixes until 2027-04-30 (nodejs/Release schedule). Not the newest LTS is not end of life.

entries.label: must-not-fire
entries.subject: timers/promises
entries.rationale: 'timers/promises' is a Node.js built-in module imported by its bare name (without the node: prefix). It is not an npm package and must not be declared; a rule that treats every bare specifier as a package is caught.

entries.label: must-not-fire
entries.subject: uuid
entries.rationale: npm uuid 14.0.2 (2026-08-18) is not deprecated. registry.npmjs.org deprecates uuid 10 and below ('uuid@10 and below is no longer supported'); a rule that reads the package's deprecation history instead of the resolved version's is caught. (The same declaration is unused: UNU-001.)

entries.label: must-not-fire
entries.rationale: Promoted from scan 1. Strict null checking is on for every type-checking configuration: tsconfig.json extends @tsconfig/node22, whose base configuration sets "strict": true, and tsconfig.build.json extends tsconfig.json (tsc --showConfig prints "strict": true for both). A rule that reads only the options a file states itself, without resolving 'extends', is caught.

entries.label: must-not-fire
entries.rationale: Promoted from scan 1 (as in bench-ts-baseline-clean). The authorization rules are named and listable: src/http/require-terminal.ts names the three scopes, every /api route declares its scope with requireScope(Scopes.x) where it is registered, and a terminal is confined to its own depot in one place (ownRun); the README lists the scope per endpoint.

entries.label: score-band
entries.rationale: Both npm packages (the service and tools/manifest-export) commit a package-lock.json; CI installs each with npm ci. The dependency set is pinned and reproducible even though several pinned versions are bad.

entries.label: score-band
entries.rationale: Actions are pinned by commit SHA, but the repository publishes no release artifact, so there is nothing to sign or attest and no SBOM; partial posture by design, wide band (as the TypeScript and C# baselines).

entries.label: score-band
entries.rationale: Noticeably stale but not abandoned: of the service's seventeen direct production dependencies, three are a major version or more behind (date-fns three majors, axios 0.21 against 1.x, jsonwebtoken 8 against 9), the tool's only dependency is a patch behind, the rest are current.

entries.label: clean
entries.rationale: Certified free of the dependency, licence, end-of-life-platform, dependency-truthfulness and CI/image-pinning concepts this repository covers (whole file).
